Scavenging systems are used to remove anaesthetic gases from theatre and discard them safely. This is to reduce theatre pollution and possible adverse effects to operating room staff

High flow low pressure systems 

Active Scavenging = Uses a vacuum to remove anaesthetic gases from theatre 

**System**

**Collecting System **

Post APL valve, area where gas collects

**Transfer system **30mm tubing which takes gas to receiving system (different size to breathing system tubing 22mm) 

**Receiving system**

Open systems are open at the base and allow air to be entrained

- With excessive -ve pressure air can be entrained to prevent fluctuations in pressure
- With excessive +ve pressure air moves out to prevent pressure fluctuations

**Disposal system**

- Connects to receiving system
- Contains a device (e.g. fan) to cause a vacuum
- Can remove 30 – 130 L/min gas
- Causes gas to move from the receiving system to the disposal system 

Connected to a pipe out of theatre to discard safely

Safety Features

- Requires energy for the disposal system
